analysis: The PR changes documentation only, in two files. In docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md, the head text bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and adds lines 15-22. The new text describes deadline-estimator corrections (the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES switch, per-row decode charge at the configured MTP width, and `calibratedPathProven` still separating two conversions). It states that these need no timing-catalog entry. In docs/developer/test.md, the head adds a "Deadline Admission Estimators" section (lines 373-401). It lists test suites (EngineMeasurementOrderingTests, AdmissionRateEstimatorTests, CBv2PerBatchDecode*) and a swift test command, and says they use scripted engines with synthetic usage and no GPU or Metal. The base text of test.md was not supplied, but the patch excerpt is complete. Nothing else in either file changed. The diff adds no code, secrets, endpoints, key handling, attestation paths, receipt policy or authorization logic. Nothing touches the provider/coordinator wire, App Attest (TB-011, T-052..T-058), the encrypted prefix-cache storage (T-041), or the key assets. The docs explicitly keep "no hardware scheduling authority", the empty deadline catalog, and the requirement for independent qualification, so they do not overclaim qualification or relax a control. The one unverified contract is that the described estimator code changes (in other files, not supplied) actually match the documented behavior. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not evidence of a security regression. The deadline-admission estimator affects availability and admission, not confidentiality or authorization, as far as the supplied text shows. No findings.
